title: Korean elections: South Korean presidential elections since 1987 and North Korean official returns

south.provider: National Election Commission, Election Statistics System (info.nec.go.kr), 투·개표 > 개표현황, 대통령선거, 시도별 (cityCode=0)
south.method: Province rows of each NEC count table. Shares are of valid votes; turnout is ballots cast over registered voters. Gwangju and South Jeolla, which voted separately, are shown separately within Jeonnam–Gwangju; Gwangju is drawn from its five districts in dist/data/korea-boundaries.bin. Daejeon (1987), Ulsan (1987, 1992) and Sejong (before 2012) show the division their area voted in.

north.provider: KCNA and Central Election Committee returns, as cited per election
north.method: Officially reported national figures only. The Central Election Committee and KCNA publish no per-province results for these elections, so every province is shown with the national figure. Candidates are nominated on one approved list of the Democratic Front for the Reunification of Korea, one per constituency (some local constituencies had two in 2023).
